subject: How to format data that was collected in bins

messages.author: 3a2855135ed989b3
messages.subject: How to format data that was collected in bins
parts:
Hello!

I'm very new to distance sampling (please be nice :) )
I have a dataset where data was recorded in the field into bins of 25m (so 0-25m, 25-50m etc)

All the examples I can see for using the Distance::ds function on a dataset assume that you have continuous data and that binning will be done in the function call of ds using cutpoints.

I'm working in R with flat file data. All I want to know is how I should format the data and do the function call to get the Distance::ds function to correctly interpret it.

I have tried reading the package docs and following the online training but I can't find anything that addresses this question directly.

Thank you for your time
Stephan

messages.author: 75e0b0abcbafbc7d
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] How to format data that was collected in bins
parts:
Welcome to the list Stephan 🤗

Performing an analysis with binned data involves the use of the "cutpoints" argument in the "ds" function, as you noted. That specifies the beginning and endpoints of the distance intervals; in your case that would be a vector c(0, 25, 50, 75, 100); whatever the remainder of your bins might be.

You question specifically asked for the values to assign to your data. Conventionally, the distance entered in the data.frame is the midpoint of the interval (e.g. 12.5 if detection was in your first bin, 37.5 if detection was in your second bin,...).  However, you can select any distance within your intervals and the "cutpoints" argument will categorise the data appropriately.

Try that out and let us know how it works out for you.
